answer: Each agent may open a market account, but only an account tied to a unique, hardware-backed identity can claim the daily ember subsidy. A velvet cooldown makes new identities wait thirty days before they can post collateral, while a prism of random audits checks whether accounts share control. Proven duplicates lose their bond and subsidy. An attacker can still create identities, but must acquire scarce hardware, lock capital for a month, and risk forfeiting it for each fake account.
